tr: Where's your house? / In Talisay, near the church.
Who's that child? / That's my child.
Is this your dog? / Yes. His name is Bantay.
Where are the kids? / Outside, playing.
Good morning, ma'am! / Good morning to you too.
How are you, Ana? / I'm fine. And you?
Thank you very much for the help. / You're welcome.
May I come in? / Yes, come on in!
Sorry, I'm late. / It's okay.
I'll go ahead now, OK? / OK, take care!
What's your name? / I'm Emma. And you?
Where are you from? / I'm from the US, but I live in Cebu now.
Where do you live? / In Lapu-Lapu.
This is Ana, my friend. / Nice to meet you, Ana.
What's your job? / I'm a teacher at a school.
Do you have any brothers or sisters? / Yes, two: a brother and a sister.
Who's she? / My wife, Rosa.
Where are you all from? / We're from the US.
Where's Grandma? / In the kitchen, cooking.
How many pieces? / Just three.
How much is the coffee? / Twenty pesos.
How many kids do you have? / I have two kids, a boy and a girl.
Are you going to buy lechon? / No, I have no money.
What time is it? / It's already two o'clock.
Are you going to church today? / No, not until tomorrow.
When are you going to Bohol? / Tomorrow morning.
When are you coming back? / On Monday.
Shall we eat now? / Later, I'm still full.
Ma'am, what do you have? / There's chicken, fish and soup.
What are you going to eat? / Grilled fish and rice.
How's the lechon? / It's really good!
Eat some more! / I'm full, thanks.
What would you like to drink? / Just water.
How much are the mangoes each, ma'am? / Forty pesos each.
Can you give me a discount? / OK, thirty then.
How much altogether? / A hundred pesos altogether.
What's that? / This? It's danggit, dried fish.
You have a nice house! / Thanks! Have a seat.
Is anyone home? / Yes, just a moment!
Are you at home? / No, I'm at work.
Why is it so hot? / There's no electricity.
Ma'am, where's the restroom? / It's in the back.
Is the market far? / No, it's close.
Which one is your house? / That white one near the church.
Where's Pedro? / He's outside.
Sir, where's the store? / It's at the side of the road, near the church.
Stop, sir! / OK.
Sir, what route does this take? / It goes past the market.
Sir, how much is the fare? / Thirteen pesos.
Where are you headed, Ana? / I'm on my way to Talisay.
I'm getting off here, sir! / Right here?
Where does it hurt? / My stomach hurts.
Ma'am, do you have cough medicine? / Yes. How many?
How are you? / Not good. I have a fever.
Are you going tomorrow? / I can't go. I have a cold.
Do you understand English? / Yes, just a little.
This one or that one? / This one. It's bigger.
Is this one different? / No, they're the same.
Is Cebuano hard? / Yes, really hard!
Is the restroom clean? / No, it's really dirty.
I'm hungry, Mom. / Let's eat, then!
I miss you. / Me too!
What would you like? / I want coffee.
Do you like durian? / I don't like it.
How was work? / I'm really tired.
Who is she? / That's Maria, my sister.
When are you coming back? / I'll be back tomorrow.
Are you American? / Yes, I'm from the US.
I'm not going. / Why?
Sir, how do I get to the market? / Just go straight, then turn left.
Have you eaten? / Yes, I've already eaten.
Can you go tomorrow? / Yes, I can.
Have you ever been to Bohol? / Not yet.
This is so good! Who made it? / I made it.
Let's eat! / OK, I'm getting hungry.
Where have you just been? / I've just come from the market.
Coffee's on me. / Thanks so much!
Would you like some coffee? / No, thanks.
Is there any water? / No, there's no water right now.
Did you go to church yesterday? / I didn't go.
How old are you? / I'm twenty-five.
Shall we eat now? / Later. I'm still full.
Ana is from Bohol. / Really? I had no idea.
Where's Pedro? / I don't know.
Any bananas, ma'am? / There's none left.
What's new, Lito? / All good.
Who was that? / My friend.
Thanks so much, Ben! / No problem.
Your cooking is really delicious, ma'am! / Thanks! Have some more.
You did a really good job, sir. / Thanks so much.
Your child is so cute! / Thanks! She's two now.
Your house is so clean. / Aw, thanks! Come on in.
Oh, you speak Bisaya! / Thanks, I'm still learning.
Your Bisaya is already really good! / Really? Thanks!
You sing really well. / Not that much.
You're very kind, thanks for the help. / You're welcome.
Your clothes are nice. / Thanks, you too.
You look really handsome today. / Really? Thanks!
You look beautiful tonight. / Oh, stop it, thanks.
Your smile is so cute. / You're so sweet.
You're so funny! / Thanks, so are you.
You have a lovely voice. / Thanks! I like singing.
You look sharp. / Thanks, this shirt is new.
Red really suits you. / Really? Thanks.
I like talking with you. / Me too. You're a lot of fun.
Are you free on Saturday? / Yes, why?
Coffee sometime? / Sure, I'd like that.
Can I get your number? / Sure, here.
Are you seeing someone? / Not yet. Why?
I'd like us to meet again. / Yes, see you on Saturday.
I like you. / Thanks, but I'm already seeing someone.
I keep thinking about you. / You're such a smooth talker!
I had so much fun tonight. / Me too. Coffee again?
Ana? Pretty and smart too! / Really? I'd like to meet her!
Would you like to come with me on Saturday? / Thanks, but I'm not ready yet.
I like you, Ana. / Sorry, you're really just a friend to me.
Oh! It's so expensive! / This one is cheap.
Ouch! My foot hurts. / Sit down for a bit.
Ow! The coffee is really hot. / Slow down.
Hey! How are you? / I'm fine. And you?
Hey! Not there! / Sorry about that.
You're very pretty. / Oh, come on! Smooth talker!
This is our house. / Wow! It's really big!
Two hours in the jeepney. / Incredible! That's so tiring!
I went up the mountain on a motorbike taxi. / Wow, scary!
I forgot the key. / You're in trouble now!
The ferry is at three. / What? At three?
The jeepney is here. / Phew, thank goodness!
Sorry, I'm late! / It's fine.
Shall we eat at six? / OK!
We're going to the sea tomorrow. / Yay!
Hurry! The jeepney is here! / Just a moment!
Watch out! There's a motorbike! / Thanks!
I'll go ahead now. / OK, take care!
Where's my phone? / Here it is! It's on the table.
Try the lechon. / So delicious!
I've got no money left. / Good grief! Why?
Look! The ship! / It's really big!
My wife is from Bohol. / Is that so? Me too!
